## Wage-boundary sets and symmetric difference

- MATLAB upper: `['河北', '上海', '江苏', '浙江', '山东', '河南', '广东']`; Python upper: `['江苏', '浙江', '山东', '河南', '广东']`.

## MATLAB chronology availability audit

`matlab_calendar2009_stationary_output.mat` contains final `st/results`/`st/grids` and numerical iteration settings only; it has no 184-turn provincial state/history dataset. `matlab_profile_summary.mat` is a profiler MAT file with terminal `{status, household_call_count, outer_turn_call_count}` and profiler `FunctionTable`/`FunctionHistory`, not provincial controller states. `matlab_terminal_status.json` likewise has only terminal counts/status. Therefore no source-comparable MATLAB turn trace exists.

## Supported findings and unsupported hypotheses

Supported: representation is already repaired; final aligned evidence establishes a one-low-action Zhejiang controller-count signature and the wage-upper categorical mismatch. Chronological first divergence is unavailable. Unsupported: a MATLAB/Python fault attribution; an exact MATLAB divergence turn; a household-solver bug from Ct/At/Bt differences; a wage-clipping bug; or a claim that either model is wrong.
